q1.answer: Only 3/18 persistent Class-A intervals ever expose any one-step capacity-restoring move from the current visible hand. The affected seeds are 2024, 2034, and 2098; the other 15 persistent intervals never expose such a move at any audited visible-hand state.

q2.answer: The discriminator is very strong descriptively: persistent Class A has 5/459 one-step-recoverable visible states (1.09%), versus 14/18 (77.78%) in earlier naturally recovered Class-A intervals and 10/14 (71.43%) in winning recovered intervals.

q3.answer: When recovery is locally available inside persistent intervals, it is cheap but rare: the five states have score gaps 0, 0, 100, 100, 100; two restoring moves are already global-best. Canonical V4 defers recovery in all 5/5 states. This shows a real local miss on three seeds, but it has insufficient reach over the 18 persistent failures.

q4.answer: Naturally recovered intervals restore capacity by ordinary placement, never by equipment collection. All 17 canonical recovery selections (12 earlier Class-A + 5 winning) occur at a state where the chosen restoring move is global-best. Earlier Class-A recoveries are 8 flat-topology placements, 3 consolidations, and 1 branch; winning recoveries are 4 flat placements and 1 branch. Some trajectories defer an available recovery first: 2 deferrals in earlier Class A and 5 in winning controls.

q5.answer: Yes, successful/reversible zero states look very different from persistent failure states, but the difference falsifies the proposed recovery preference as a broad repair. All 12 earlier recovered Class-A intervals and all 5 winning zero intervals eventually expose restoring moves, and each reaches a state where recovery is global-best. By contrast only 3/18 persistent intervals ever expose any restoring move. Winning trajectories can also defer available recovery (5 deferrals across seeds 2238, 2282, 2371) and still recover, so immediate recovery preference is not failure-specific.

Successful trajectories also defer available recovery moves and still win, so an immediate recovery preference is not failure-specific.

state_semantics.one_step_exit_capacity_recoverable: At least one currently legal move from the current visible hand, applied once to a geometry-only clone with no future draw contents inspected, results in positive EXIT legal-move capacity.
state_semantics.refresh_visibility_rule: A refresh that keeps the board/state turn unchanged but changes the visible hand is recorded as a new auditable visible state.

unresolved_risks: All evidence is already-spent diagnostic data; no holdout, population win-rate, or inferential claim is justified.
Each alternative recovery move was evaluated for exactly one cloned move; no depth-2 or longer hypothetical sequence was searched.
The negative classification concerns a post-loss recovery preference. It does not refute prevention of persistent terminal-space closure before the last EXIT-compatible placement is destroyed.
Three persistent seeds do expose rare cheap restoring moves that V4 ignores, but that minority mechanism does not cover the dominant 18-seed Class-A failure mode.
